questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of Java Streams?
options: A) Storing data in a mutable collection.
B) Performing operations on sequences of elements in a declarative way.
C) Creating new threads for parallel processing.
questions.correctOption: B) Performing operations on sequences of elements in a declarative way.
questions.explanation: Java Streams provide a functional and declarative way to process sequences of elements, enabling operations like filtering, mapping, and reducing data.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about a Java Stream is true after a terminal operation (e.g., collect, forEach) has been performed on it?
options: A) It can be reused for subsequent operations.
B) It can be modified by adding or removing elements.
C) It is closed and cannot be used again.
D) It automatically converts into a new collection.
questions.correctOption: C) It is closed and cannot be used again.
questions.explanation: Java Streams are designed to be single-use. Once a terminal operation is executed, the stream is considered consumed and cannot be traversed again.
